question: Ravikirti's Aihole inscription speaks in detail the victory of Pulakesin II over:
solution:
The correct answer is __**Harsha**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Aihole inscription**

 
 
• During Pulakeshi II's rule, poet **Ravikirti** created the** Aihole inscription**.
 
• Aihole, which is in the state of **Karnataka**, is well known as the birthplace of Indian architecture.
 
• It served as the **Chalukyas' capital**.
 
• This inscription details Pulakesin's achievements, particularly how he fought **Harshavardhana**.
 
• **Harshavardhana was defeated by Pulakeshin II**, the King of the Chalukya dynasty when he attempted to expand his Empire towards the southern peninsula of India.
 
• On the banks of the River Narmada, Pulakesin II had beaten Harshavardhan in **618 AD**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• In the construction of structure temples, the Chalukyan developed the **Deccan or Vesara style** in the buildings.
 
• They mastered the **technique for stone construction**, which involves joining stones carefully without mortar.
 
• Aihole provides important details on the early history of the **Badami Chalukyas up until 634 AD**, as well as the birth and death dates of the poets K**alidasa and Bharavi**.
 
• It is highly commendable to the poet named **Ravikirti **who wrote the song.
 
• Its final verse is crucial to the history of **Sanskrit literature**.
 
• It states that Ravikirti, the record's author, has achieved the **fame of Kalidasa and Bharavi through his poetic talent**.
